audit.whatIsWrong: Two rows contradicted their own whys and the packet: level 6 was given to Graves at 3/10 while whys[4] read 'Illaoi-favoured', and 2+ items was given to Illaoi at 6/10 while whys[6] read 'Graves-favoured'.
audit.why: Packet chart and the audited mirror both read Skill at level 6 and Graves at 2+ items.
audit.corrected: Level 6 -> Skill 5/10, 2+ items -> Graves 3/10 (inverse of the mirror's 7/10), proposed as one atomic group across both layers, with whys[4] and both phase reasons rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and 2+ item phases carried the generic boilerplate with no timing.
audit.why: Leap of Faith is 120s at rank 1 and spawns one tentacle per champion hit; Collateral Damage is 100s at 1000 range, which is exactly why 6 is even rather than Illaoi's.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[6].why now name both ultimates' cooldowns and the real 2+ item takeover.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every line said 'engage when Quickdraw is down' as if it were a fixed window. It is not: hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers Quickdraw's cooldown and refreshes the resistance boost, so against a farming Graves it is rarely fully down.
audit.why: Riot's own text on Quickdraw. Also: dashing toward a champion grants two stacks of True Grit instead of one, so his armour is highest exactly when he engages you.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now state the 16s base, the auto-attack refund and the double True Grit stacks.

audit.why: Riot's text says it reduces sight range and briefly slows on impact — there is no blind. The mirror removed the same claim from its own page.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the vision cut and the slow.

edits.before: Leap of Faith inside your tentacle field is a 1v3 button. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Graves's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Even at 6: Leap of Faith is 120s and spawns a tentacle per champion hit, but Collateral Damage at 100s answers it from 1000 range.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Graves carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items and it is his: Quickdraw's cooldown drops on every auto, so he kites clear of the tentacles and shoots from outside.

edits.before: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Quickdraw (E): 16s at rank 1, but every auto he lands cuts it — it is rarely fully down, so trade when he has just used it. - Smoke Screen (W): 26s. - Harsh Lesson (W): flat 4s. - Leap of Faith: 120s, kill windows only.

edits.before: His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Quickdraw is 16s but autos refund it, and dashing at you gives him two True Grit stacks.

edits.before: Track Graves's Quickdraw: His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. When it is down — Land E, slam the spirit.
edits.after: Quickdraw refunds cooldown on every auto he lands, so it is rarely truly down — commit the moment he spends it.

edits.before: Illaoi-favoured: R Leap of Faith forces him to trade inside the ring where slams win.
edits.after: Skill: level 6 is even — your tentacle ring versus his 100s Collateral Damage.

edits.before: W Smoke Screen to blind and disengage your all-in
edits.after: W Smoke Screen cuts your vision and slows you

notes: The page's central instruction — 'engage when Quickdraw is down' — was misleading: Quickdraw's cooldown is refunded by his basic attacks, so a farming Graves almost never has it fully down. Retargeted onto the moment he spends it. Also removed the Smoke Screen blind claim (Riot's text says sight reduction plus a brief slow), matching the mirror. Per the mirror's flag, nothing here asserts that Leap of Faith grounds Quickdraw — the kit file's derived grounding flag is not supported by Riot's R description.
